title: Reinforcement Learning & the AI Frontier of Prescriptive Analytics
subtitle: Agents that learn to decide — from Q-learning intuition to RL running live on a million SKUs, plus LLM copilots that write your models

objectives.title: Build Q-learning intuition
objectives.description: Understand states, actions, rewards, and the Q-table well enough to explain how an agent learns an ordering policy from trial and error — no forecasting model required.

objectives.title: Study RL that is actually deployed
objectives.description: Ground the hype in numbers: Alibaba's DeepStock running live on 100% of over 1 million SKU-warehouse pairs, Amazon's deep RL across 10,000+ SKUs, and DoorDash's multi-agent RL dispatch.

objectives.title: Meet the LLM optimization copilots
objectives.description: See how OptiMUS and Gurobi AI Modeling turn natural-language business problems into working solver code — and what that means for your career as the person who checks the model.

objectives.title: Assemble the modern prescriptive stack

agenda.title: Opening: The Model That Never Forecasts
agenda.description: Last week we predicted, then decided. Tonight's twist: reinforcement learning collapses the two stages into one — an agent that learns good decisions directly from experience and reward.
bulletPoints: From predict-then-optimize to learn-to-act: what changes and why it matters
The MDP frame you already know from earlier sessions, now with learning
Tonight's arc: intuition, deployed proof, LLM copilots, then the whole course in one picture

agenda.title: Q-Learning in Plain English
agenda.description: The single most teachable RL algorithm: keep a table of how good each action is in each state, act, observe the reward, and nudge the table toward the truth. Repeat until wise.
bulletPoints: States, actions, rewards — the inventory manager's day as an MDP
The Q-table as an evolving cheat sheet of decision quality
Exploration vs. exploitation: why the agent must sometimes order 'wrong' on purpose
The update rule in one line, and what the learning rate and discount factor really mean

agenda.title: Deployed RL: The Numbers Behind the Stories
agenda.description: RL is not a lab curiosity anymore — it is running supply chains tonight. Three deployed systems, with scale and stakes attached.
bulletPoints: Alibaba DeepStock: RL live on 100% of 1M+ SKU-warehouse pairs since October 2025
Amazon Deep Inventory Management: deep RL making replenishment decisions across 10,000+ SKUs
DoorDash: multi-agent RL dispatching drivers to orders in real time
The pattern: massive repeated decisions, fast feedback, simulators to train in safely

agenda.title: Break
agenda.description: Breathe — the second half brings LLM copilots, a hands-on RL lab, and the course finale synthesis.

agenda.title: LLMs as Optimization Copilots
agenda.description: The newest layer of the stack: language models that read a business problem in English and draft the optimization model for you. Your job shifts from typing constraints to judging them.
bulletPoints: OptiMUS (ICML 2024): natural language in, formulated and solved MILP out
Gurobi AI Modeling: prompt-to-gurobipy workflows from the solver company itself
Microsoft won the 2026 Edelman Award by combining ML, optimization, and agentic AI — the stack is the story
The new scarce skill: knowing when the copilot's model is wrong

agenda.title: Lab: Teach an Agent to Run the Stockroom
agenda.description: In Colab, build a tiny Gymnasium inventory environment and watch a Q-learning agent go from ordering at random to discovering a sensible base-stock-style policy — with zero demand forecasts.
bulletPoints: Define the environment: inventory state, order actions, profit-minus-holding-cost reward
Run the Q-learning loop and watch average reward climb
Inspect the learned Q-table: what policy did the agent invent?

agenda.title: Course Synthesis: The Modern Prescriptive Stack
agenda.description: Zoom out on the whole semester: LP to IP to networks to MDPs to deep learning to RL is not six topics — it is one toolkit, and you now own all of it. Final project briefing closes the night.
bulletPoints: One map: which tool for which decision, from deterministic to sequential-under-uncertainty
How the pieces compose: forecasts feed solvers, solvers seed simulators, RL closes the loop
Final project prep: presentation format, the dollars-quantified requirement, and next week's run of show

activities.title: Q-Learning the Stockroom: An Agent Learns to Order
activities.description: Build a miniature inventory world with Gymnasium and let a Q-learning agent loose in it. Starting from pure randomness, the agent discovers an ordering policy purely from reward — the same core loop that Alibaba and Amazon run at planetary scale.

steps.title: Build the environment
steps.description: Create a small Gymnasium env: state is on-hand inventory (0-20), actions are order quantities (0-10), reward is sales revenue minus ordering and holding costs, demand arrives randomly each day.

steps.title: Run the learning loop
steps.description: Train for 5,000 simulated days with epsilon-greedy exploration, updating the Q-table after every step and decaying exploration over time.

steps.title: Watch the policy emerge
steps.description: Plot average reward per 100 episodes — the climb is the learning. Then read the greedy policy off the Q-table row by row.

steps.title: Stress-test the agent
steps.description: Change the demand distribution or holding cost, retrain, and see the policy adapt — no reformulation, no new forecast, just new experience.

codeBlock.code:
import numpy as np
import gymnasium as gym

env = TinyInventoryEnv()          # states: inventory 0-20, actions: order 0-10
Q = np.zeros((21, 11))            # the agent's cheat sheet
alpha, gamma, eps = 0.1, 0.95, 1.0

for episode in range(5000):
    s, _ = env.reset()
    done = False
    while not done:
        a = env.action_space.sample() if np.random.rand() < eps \
            else int(np.argmax(Q[s]))
        s2, r, done, trunc, _ = env.step(a)
        # one-line Q-learning update: nudge toward reward + future value
        Q[s, a] += alpha * (r + gamma * np.max(Q[s2]) - Q[s, a])
        s = s2
    eps = max(0.05, eps * 0.999)  # explore less as we grow wise

policy = np.argmax(Q, axis=1)
print("Learned ordering policy by inventory level:", policy)

activities.discussionNote: Look at the learned policy together: the agent typically orders a lot when inventory is low and nothing when shelves are full — it has rediscovered base-stock logic no one taught it. Discuss: for which decisions in your own company is there enough repetition and feedback for this loop to work, and where would letting an agent explore be unacceptable?

takeaways.text: Reinforcement learning collapses predict-then-optimize into learn-to-act — and it is already running live on millions of real inventory decisions at Alibaba, Amazon, and DoorDash.
LLM copilots like OptiMUS and Gurobi AI Modeling now draft optimization models from plain English. Your edge is no longer typing the model — it is judging it.
LP, IP, networks, MDPs, deep learning, and RL are one stack, not six topics. Microsoft's 2026 Edelman win came from combining them — and now you can too.
